question: Compute Spearman's rank correlation between microbiome diversity (Shannon index) and inflammatory marker (CRP) across 120 patients. Test significance of correlation and return the Spearman's rho value, p-value, and 95% confidence interval.

files.eval_guideline: Spearman rho must match within +/-0.01; CI bounds must match within +/-0.05; p-value must match within +/-0.001; column order and header labels may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename spearman_correlation_results.csv and CSV format. They belong to the same task and clearly correspond to the requested Spearman correlation results for Shannon diversity and CRP.

parameters.question: Compare Spearman correlation results by aligning equivalent fields despite differing header labels or column order. Require rho within +/-0.01, p-value within +/-0.001, and each 95% confidence interval bound within +/-0.05.

files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires value-by-value matching of a small results table with explicit numeric tolerances while allowing column order and header labels to differ. Approximate comparison supports this alignment, including any variation from confidence interval estimation.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables contain one aggregate correlation result in the same orientation. Map the four reference metrics by exact column names and exclude the candidate's extra N and Method metadata columns. There are no identifying columns; the single result rows correspond positionally, so row alignment and sorting are unnecessary. All reported numeric differences fall within the specified tolerances.

column_configs.name: Spearman_Rho
column_configs.reasoning: The requested correlation estimate is critical. Convert the absolute tolerance of 0.01 to reference-relative error: 0.01 / 0.4147.

column_configs.name: P_Value
column_configs.reasoning: The p-value is required to assess significance. Convert the specified absolute tolerance of 0.001 to reference-relative error: 0.001 / 0.000002 = 500. The large relative tolerance follows from the very small reference p-value.

column_configs.name: CI_Lower
column_configs.reasoning: The lower 95% confidence bound is required. Convert the absolute tolerance of 0.05 to reference-relative error: 0.05 / 0.2474.

column_configs.name: CI_Upper
column_configs.reasoning: The upper 95% confidence bound is required. Convert the absolute tolerance of 0.05 to reference-relative error: 0.05 / 0.5579.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: Compare all four requested float64 statistics using cellwise RAE; computing Pearson or Spearman correlation between single-row outputs would be inappropriate. Tolerances assume RAE = abs(candidate - reference) / abs(reference), translating the guideline's absolute tolerances into relative thresholds using the supplied reference values. All four candidate statistics satisfy these tolerances. Exclude candidate-only N and Method because they are supplementary metadata. Column order and header variations are handled by alignment; no categorical parsing is needed.
